model_constitutive: Double-porosity (matrix pores + penny-shaped fractures) viscoelastic-like attenuated Biot poroelasticity with depth-exponentially heterogeneous shear modulus and density
geometry: (n-1) horizontally stratified cracked porous layers overlying a heterogeneous fractured porous half-space
method: Haskell transfer-matrix complex dispersion derivation combined with explicit finite-difference von Neumann Courant-number stability and numerical dispersion/group-velocity analysis
main_result: Derives complex SH-wave dispersion and damping relations in multilayered fractured porous media, confirming SH dispersion is independent of matrix/fracture pore fluid pressures while strongly sensitive to total porosity, exponential heterogeneity, and FD grid discretization ratio
validation: Reduces to classical N-layer Love wave dispersion for non-porous homogeneous isotropic layers
stated_limitations: Antiplane SH polarization decouples completely from pore-fluid pressure dynamics; isothermal linear geophysical model
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: SH-wave propagation in linearly varying fiber-reinforced viscoelastic composite structure under initial stress
authors: Sumit Kumar Vishwakarma; Tapas Ranjan Panigrahi; Rupinderjit Kaur
model_constitutive: Biot incremental elastodynamics for pre-stressed Spencer-type linearly heterogeneous fiber-reinforced Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic layer over a pre-stressed heterogeneous viscoelastic half-space
geometry: Finite-thickness fiber-reinforced viscoelastic layer (-H <= x_2 <= 0) bonded to an inhomogeneous pre-stressed viscoelastic half-space (x_2 >= 0)
method: Whittaker confluent hypergeometric function exact ODE solution in depth yielding closed-form complex Love-type dispersion equation
main_result: Obtains exact Whittaker-function dispersion and damped-velocity relations, showing initial compressive/tensile stresses in layer (zeta_1) vs substrate (zeta_2) exert opposite shifts on SH phase and damped velocities
validation: Reduces to classical homogeneous elastic Love-wave equation when heterogeneity, fiber reinforcement, viscosity, and initial stresses vanish
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear antiplane SH mode only; Kelvin-Voigt viscosity has unbounded high-frequency speed; no experimental validation
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Characteristic analysis of seismic wave propagation at the free surface under the second-order strain gradient theory
authors: Zhi-Yang Wang et al. (Institute of Geology and Geophysics, CAS / BUCT)
model_constitutive: Isotropic Mindlin/Aifantis-type second-order strain gradient (SSG) elastodynamics incorporating microstructural characteristic length scales into 2D P-SV seismic wave equations and higher-order traction-free surface boundary conditions
geometry: 2D homogeneous and complex-layered geological half-spaces with planar traction-free top surface and CPML absorbing lateral/bottom boundaries
method: Plane-wave/Rayleigh dispersion analysis combined with high-order optimized staggered-grid finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) seismic wavefield modeling and CPML
main_result: Demonstrates that microstructural strain-gradient scale parameters make free-surface Rayleigh waves dispersive even in a homogeneous half-space, lowering Rayleigh phase velocity as frequency and microstructural length scale increase
validation: Zero-length-scale FDTD seismograms verified against classical elastic Rayleigh/body-wave benchmarks
stated_limitations: 2D isothermal purely elastic strain-gradient formulation without viscoelastic attenuation, poroelasticity, or field-data inversion
future_work: Incorporate SSG Rayleigh dispersion effects into shallow near-surface geophysical inversion and complex geological modeling

title: Generalized Rayleigh surface waves in a piezoelectric semiconductor half space
authors: Xiaoshan Cao; Simiao Hu; Jianjun Liu; Junping Shi
model_constitutive: 2D plane-strain transversely isotropic (6mm) n-type piezoelectric semiconductor coupling elastodynamics, Gauss electrostatics, and linearized electron drift-diffusion continuity under DC bias electric field
geometry: Semi-infinite polarized 6mm piezoelectric semiconductor half-space (ZnO / CdS) with electrically open or shorted traction-free boundary
method: 4-field (u_x, u_z, phi, n) evanescent partial-wave superposition (8th-order depth polynomial) and 4x4 boundary secular determinant root tracking
main_result: Characterizes dispersive attenuated P-SV generalized Rayleigh waves in piezoelectric semiconductors, showing carrier diffusion/conduction lowers speed and induces attenuation while supercritical DC drift bias reverses attenuation into acoustic wave amplification
validation: Reduces to insulating piezoelectric Rayleigh waves as steady carrier density n_0 -> 0 and matches classical CdS/ZnO SAW benchmarks
stated_limitations: Classical local continuum (no flexoelectric/strain-gradient/surface size effects) and isothermal linearized carrier transport
future_work: Design active amplified SAW devices using DC-biased piezoelectric semiconductors

title: Nonlocal viscoelastic medium approach to free vibrations of modified Jeffreys viscoelastic nanobeams
authors: Hayrullah Gun Kadioglu; Mustafa Ozgur Yayli
journal: International Journal of Mechanics and Materials in Design
model_constitutive: Euler-Bernoulli nanobeam governed by Romano-Barretta stress-driven nonlocal elasticity coupled with a 3-parameter modified Jeffreys viscoelastic rheology (1 elastic + 2 viscous elements), embedded in a nonlocal viscoelastic foundation
geometry: Simply supported 1D nanobeam of length L embedded in a nonlocal viscoelastic surrounding medium
method: Stress-driven nonlocal differential inversion with constitutive boundary conditions and analytical Navier sinusoidal series eigenvalue solution
main_result: Derives closed-form complex damped natural frequencies for stress-driven modified-Jeffreys viscoelastic nanobeams, showing stiffening from stress-driven beam nonlocality and flexible multi-timescale damping compared to Kelvin-Voigt and Maxwell limits
validation: Limiting-case comparisons against local elastic, Kelvin-Voigt, Maxwell, and stress-driven elastic nanobeam frequency benchmarks
stated_limitations: Restricted to simply supported boundary conditions (Navier series) and isothermal linear Euler-Bernoulli kinematics
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: A computationally efficient semi-analytical method for size-dependent free vibration of nonlocal Timoshenko nanobeams
authors: Aysegul Tepe
journal: International Journal of Mechanics and Materials in Design
model_constitutive: Eringen differential nonlocal linear Timoshenko beam theory (incorporating transverse shear deformation and rotary inertia with nonlocal parameter e_0*a)
geometry: 1D uniform Timoshenko nanobeam under clamped-clamped, simply-supported, clamped-free, and clamped-pinned boundary conditions
method: Initial Value Method (IVM) state-space transfer matrix combined with Pade rational matrix-exponential approximation
main_result: Provides a fast, mesh-free semi-analytical IVM-Pade solver for size-dependent natural frequencies of nonlocal Timoshenko nanobeams across arbitrary classical boundary conditions
validation: Benchmarked to high precision against exact analytical and published FEM/DQM nonlocal Timoshenko beam natural frequencies
stated_limitations: Uses Eringen differential nonlocal form on bounded beams (without addressing Romano et al. 2017 integral-to-differential cantilever CBCs); isothermal uniform beams only
future_work: Extend the IVM-Pade framework to functionally graded/variable-cross-section nanostructures, elastic foundations, and coupled thermal environments

title: Rayleigh Surface Waves on a Kelvin-Voigt Viscoelastic Half-Space
authors: Stan Chirita; Michele Ciarletta; Vincenzo Tibullo
model_constitutive: Isotropic linear Kelvin-Voigt viscoelasticity with depth-exponentially graded Lamé moduli, viscosities, and mass density exp(-gamma*x_2)
geometry: Homogeneous and exponentially depth-graded traction-free viscoelastic half-space x_2 >= 0
method: Exact complex secular equation formulation enforcing strict thermodynamic positivity of time-averaged viscoelastic dissipation energy to filter physical vs spurious Riemann-sheet roots
main_result: Proves via viscoelastic dissipation-energy admissibility that a Kelvin-Voigt half-space can support 1, 2, or 3 physical Rayleigh surface waves depending on viscosity ratios: when unique the surface orbit is retrograde, whereas when multiple surface waves exist one is retrograde and the extra viscosity-induced modes exhibit prograde (direct) surface orbits
validation: Recovers classical retrograde elastic Rayleigh wave as viscosities -> 0 and verifies root admissibility analytically and numerically
stated_limitations: Isothermal Kelvin-Voigt viscoelasticity (parabolic damping without finite relaxation time); exponential grading shares identical exponent gamma across all parameters
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Rayleigh wave propagation in an elastic half-space with an attached piezoelectric semiconductor layer considering flexoelectricity and size-effects
authors: Linyao Wang; Aibing Zhang; Chuanzeng Zhang; Jianke Du; Z. M. Xiao; Jia Lou
model_constitutive: Size-dependent transversely isotropic piezoelectric semiconductor (PSC) continuum incorporating flexoelectricity, strain gradients (l_1), electric-field gradients (l_2), dynamic micro-inertia gradients (l_0), and linearized carrier drift-diffusion under 2D bias electric fields
geometry: Finite-thickness n-type ZnO PSC thin layer bonded atop a semi-infinite isotropic/anisotropic elastic substrate
method: Higher-order coupled partial-wave eigenvalue expansion in the PSC layer matched to evanescent substrate modes under classical + higher-order traction/polarization/carrier interface conditions
main_result: Quantifies competing nanoscale size effects on layered Rayleigh SAW: strain gradient l_1 and flexoelectricity stiffen and raise phase speed, whereas inertia gradient l_0 and electric-field gradient l_2 lower phase speed, and horizontal supercritical bias electric fields switch attenuation to Rayleigh-wave amplification
validation: Reduces accurately to classical layered piezoelectric and local PSC Rayleigh dispersion curves when gradient lengths and flexoelectricity vanish
stated_limitations: Isothermal linearized small-carrier-perturbation model (neglects Joule heating and non-Fourier thermoelastic coupling despite bias currents)
future_work: Guide design of nanoscale flexoelectric/piezotronic SAW amplifiers and sensors

title: Surface wave transference in a piezoelectric cylinder coated with reinforced material
authors: K. K. Pankaj; S. A. Sahu; S. Kumari
model_constitutive: Linear pre-stressed transversely isotropic piezoelectric core coupled via mechanical spring-type imperfect interface to a pre-stressed Spencer self-reinforced elastic coating
geometry: Solid pre-stressed piezoelectric cylinder (0 <= r <= r_1) coated by a concentric finite-thickness fiber-reinforced outer shell (r_1 <= r <= r_2) under open/shorted outer electrical BCs
method: Circumferential/axial SH Bessel/Neumann potential analytical expansion yielding closed-form secular determinant
main_result: Shows mechanical interface imperfection markedly lowers SH phase velocity while fiber reinforcement, thickness ratio, initial stress, and piezoelectric stiffening provide strong tunability
validation: Analytical reduction to classical concentric isotropic Love-like cylindrical dispersion when piezoelectricity, initial stress, reinforcement, and interface compliance vanish
stated_limitations: Isothermal decoupled SH mode without experimental data
future_work: Apply to cylindrical smart-material SAW resonator optimization

title: Statics of FGM circular plate with magneto-electro-elastic coupling: axisymmetric solutions and their relations with those for corresponding rectangular beam
authors: Yanzheng Wang; Weiqiu Chen; Xiangyu Li
model_constitutive: Exact 3D linear transversely isotropic functionally graded magneto-electro-elasticity (FGMEE) with arbitrary through-thickness material variation c(z)
geometry: Axisymmetric FGM magneto-electro-elastic circular plate vs plane-stress/plane-strain FGM rectangular beam under normal surface loads
method: Direct 3D displacement/potential polynomial-in-r expansion (without plate kinematic hypotheses) and exact algebraic correspondence mapping to 2D beam solutions
main_result: Establishes exact 3D analytical axisymmetric solutions for FGMEE circular plates and proves universal correspondence relations expressing 3D FGMEE plate fields directly in terms of corresponding 2D FGM beam fields whenever all moduli share identical z-grading
validation: Verified against homogeneous and exponentially graded piezoelectric/magneto-electro-elastic 3D plate benchmarks
stated_limitations: Static isothermal linear response; exact plate-beam correspondence requires proportional through-thickness grading across all coupled moduli
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: A higher-order beam theory for analyzing the static and dynamic behaviors of box and tubular beam-columns with the higher-order effect of axial force
authors: Weili Ma; Xianfang Li
model_constitutive: Higher-order shear-deformable beam-column theory derived via Hamilton's principle with cross-sectional warping function f(z), capturing higher-order coupling of initial axial tensile/compressive force N_0 on both flexural stiffness and effective rotary/translational inertia
geometry: Thin/thick-walled box and circular tubular beam-columns under axial tension/compression, static bending, buckling, and flexural vibration/wave propagation
method: Variational Hamilton-principle derivation without shear correction factor and exact analytical static deflection, critical buckling, and natural-frequency solutions
main_result: Proves that higher-order shear-warping axial-force coupling increases effective beam inertia under BOTH tensile and compressive axial loads while softening compressive buckling loads in short/thin-walled box and tubular beams relative to Timoshenko beam-column theory
validation: Validated against 3D finite-element shell/solid simulations and classical Euler-Bernoulli / Timoshenko beam-column benchmarks
stated_limitations: Macroscopic local isothermal linear incremental elasticity
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Higher-order topological states and magnetic field control in elastic metamaterials
authors: Yuqi Tang; Weijian Zhou; Yangwei Mai; Yingjie Chen; Zheng Zhong; Weiqiu Chen
model_constitutive: Magneto-mechanical incremental elasticity of a hard/soft magnetorheological elastomer (MRE) surface coating bonded to a pillared honeycomb/kagome-like elastic plate substrate under external bias magnetic field
geometry: 2D periodic/supercell pillared elastic metamaterial plate with magnetorheological surface layer (hexagonal/triangular symmetry)
method: 3D finite-element Floquet-Bloch band-structure, Wannier-center / bulk-polarization topological invariant calculation, and supercell eigenmode simulations
main_result: Realizes both 1D topologically protected valley/pseudospin Lamb-wave edge states and 0D higher-order topological corner states, demonstrating non-contact magnetic-field tuning of corner/edge frequencies and topological phase transitions
validation: Full-wave 3D FEM frequency-response and disorder/defect-immunity transmission simulations
stated_limitations: Numerical/theoretical FEM demonstration neglecting MRE viscoelastic hysteresis losses and magnetothermal heating; no experimental fabrication reported here
future_work: Experimental realization of magnetically reconfigurable higher-order topological acoustic/elastic wave devices

title: Incremental Elasticity of Pre-stretched Elastomers with Strain Hardening Effect: Half-Space and Thin-Layer Limits
authors: Le Du; Zhaohe Dai; Jianmin Long; Rui Xiao; Weiqiu Chen
model_constitutive: Small-on-large incremental incompressible nonlinear hyperelasticity using the 8-chain Arruda-Boyce strain-hardening free energy (locking stretch sqrt(N))
geometry: Equibiaxially/uniaxially pre-stretched incompressible elastomer in two asymptotic limits: semi-infinite half-space and thin layer bonded to a rigid substrate under axisymmetric Hertz-type spherical indentation
method: Incremental Biot/Ogden equations solved via Hankel/Fourier transforms and asymptotic thin-layer perturbation to derive exact surface Green's functions and indentation force-depth laws
main_result: Obtains closed-form surface Green's functions and spherical indentation force-displacement laws in both half-space and thin-film limits, showing finite-chain locking parameter N strongly amplifies incremental indentation stiffness as pre-stretch approaches chain-locking stretch (recovering neo-Hookean as N -> inf)
validation: Asymptotic half-space and thin-layer analytical formulas validated against nonlinear finite-element indentation simulations and neo-Hookean limits
stated_limitations: Static, isothermal, purely hyperelastic (neglects elastomer viscoelastic relaxation and poroelastic solvent migration)
future_work: Apply incremental Green's functions to soft-matter contact, adhesion, and surface instability problems

title: Love Waves in a Piezoelectric Semiconductor Thin Film on an Elastic Dielectric Half-Space
authors: Ru Tian; Guoquan Nie; Jinxi Liu; Ernian Pan; Yuesheng Wang
model_constitutive: Linearized 6mm n-type piezoelectric semiconductor thin film (coupled SH elastodynamics, electrostatics, and DC-biased electron drift-diffusion) perfectly bonded to an isotropic elastic dielectric half-space
geometry: Finite-thickness PSC film (-h <= x_2 <= 0) on semi-infinite elastic dielectric substrate (x_2 >= 0) with electrically open/shorted free surface
method: Exact analytical partial-wave modal synthesis across the film and evanescent substrate yielding complex Love-wave dispersion equations for the first three modes
main_result: Demonstrates semiconducting carriers make Love modes dispersive and attenuated, sharply drop phase velocity in a critical carrier-density window, shift higher-mode cutoffs slightly above substrate shear speed, and produce Love-wave amplification above a critical DC drift field
validation: Reduces to classical piezoelectric-dielectric Love wave benchmarks in the insulating limit n_0 -> 0
stated_limitations: Local isothermal continuum model neglecting nanoscale film surface/gradient effects and Joule heating under high DC bias
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: SH surface waves in piezoelectric semiconductors loaded with a finite viscous liquid layer
authors: Lele Zhang; Haocheng Guo; Jinxi Liu; Yuantai Hu
model_constitutive: Semi-infinite 6mm n-type piezoelectric semiconductor (linearized drift-diffusion current without DC bias) coupled at solid-liquid interface to a Newtonian viscous dielectric liquid layer of finite thickness h
geometry: Finite Newtonian viscous liquid layer (-h <= y <= 0) atop a semi-infinite n-type ZnO piezoelectric semiconductor half-space (y >= 0) under shorted or open interface electrical BCs
method: Exact analytical coupling of viscous shear-diffusion liquid modes and 3-field PSC evanescent modes yielding explicit complex dispersion relations
main_result: Finds peak SH attenuation at a frequency-proportional critical electron concentration, shows phase velocity transitions from elastic to insulating-piezoelectric asymptotes as frequency grows, and identifies a carrier threshold above which open vs shorted interface differences vanish
validation: Analytical limiting reductions to dry Bleustein-Gulyaev PSC waves (h -> 0) and viscous-liquid-loaded insulating piezoelectric half-spaces (n_0 -> 0)
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear small-signal model without DC bias drift, surface tension, or thermal effects
future_work: Guide liquid-phase acoustic biosensor design on piezoelectric semiconductor substrates

title: Mechanics of SH and anti-plane SH waves in orthotropic piezoelectric quasicrystal with multiple surface effect
authors: Seema; Abhinav Singhal
model_constitutive: Linear 1D-hexagonal / orthotropic piezoelectric quasicrystal (coupled phonon displacement, phason displacement, and electric potential) incorporating Gurtin-Murdoch-type surface piezoelectricity, surface elasticity, and surface residual stress
geometry: Finite-thickness orthotropic piezoelectric quasicrystal (PQC) plate and PQC thin film covering an elastic half-space
method: Exact analytical antiplane phonon-phason-electric potential partial-wave expansion and closed-form transcendental dispersion determinants under open/shorted electrical surface conditions
main_result: Determines critical nanoscale film thickness below which multiple surface piezoelectric/phason effects strongly shift SH dispersion curves (1 nm vs 10 nm vs 100 nm) across the first eight guided modes
validation: Reduces to classical transversely isotropic piezoelectric plate/Love-wave dispersion when phason coupling and surface parameters vanish
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear antiplane SH polarization only; no experimental comparison
future_work: Guide design of nanoscale orthotropic piezoelectric quasicrystal SAW detectors

title: Surface waves propagating in an elastic half-space considering both the effects of strain gradient and surface elasticity
authors: Jianmin Long; Bowen Zhao
model_constitutive: Combined isotropic Mindlin first-strain-gradient elastodynamics (5 bulk gradient moduli + micro-inertia length h) in the half-space interior and Gurtin-Murdoch surface elasticity (surface Lame moduli, residual tension, surface density) on the boundary
geometry: Homogeneous isotropic elastic half-space supporting both antiplane (SH) and in-plane (Rayleigh P-SV) surface acoustic waves
method: Higher-order bulk Helmholtz potential decomposition coupled to non-classical surface-stress + double-traction boundary conditions, deriving explicit phase-velocity bounds and dispersion curves
main_result: Establishes exact phase-velocity bounds for antiplane and in-plane surface waves under simultaneous strain-gradient and surface-elasticity effects, showing large dynamic micro-inertia length h creates a high-wavenumber stopband (low-pass filter) for antiplane surface waves while k -> 0 recovers classical Rayleigh speed
validation: Recovers pure Gurtin-Murdoch surface-wave dispersion and pure Mindlin strain-gradient Rayleigh dispersion in respective limits
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear isotropic half-space without thermoelastic or viscoelastic dissipation
future_work: Design wavenumber-selective nanoscale acoustic low-pass surface-wave filters

title: Propagation characteristics of SH waves in piezoelectric-piezomagnetic sandwich structures
authors: Ruomeng Tian; Xiongxiong Liang; Yijia Shi; Ru Tian; Jinxi Liu
model_constitutive: Linear coupled magneto-electro-elasticity in symmetric 6mm piezoelectric (PE) / piezomagnetic (PM) / piezoelectric (PE) laminates
geometry: Three-layer symmetric PE/PM/PE finite-thickness sandwich plate with perfectly bonded interfaces and electromagnetically open/shorted outer faces
method: Symmetric/antisymmetric antiplane SH modal decomposition and exact analytical dispersion equations across BaTiO3/CoFe2O4 and PZT/Terfenol-D material pairs
main_result: Demonstrates SH mode cutoffs and high-k asymptotes are controlled by the ordering of PE/PM bulk shear speeds and PE Bleustein-Gulyaev surface wave speeds, with PE/PM thickness ratio strongly tuning low-order modes
validation: Limiting-case checks as core or face-sheet thickness ratios tend to zero or infinity
stated_limitations: Isothermal perfectly bonded local continuum model
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Effects of interfacial elasticity on the reflection and refraction of SH waves
authors: Jianmin Long; Hui Fan
model_constitutive: Two isotropic linear elastic half-spaces separated by a non-ideal coherent interface modeled both by Gurtin-Murdoch interfacial elasticity and by a strain-gradient thin-membrane interphase
geometry: Planar non-ideal elastic interface z = 0 between two dissimilar semi-infinite elastic media under obliquely incident harmonic SH plane waves
method: Analytical boundary-jump amplitude matching for complex reflection/transmission coefficients, phase jumps, and energy-flux conservation
main_result: Proves interfacial elasticity and interphase strain gradients increase SH reflection, reduce transmission, introduce non-zero reflection/transmission phase shifts even below the critical angle, and trigger sharp phase jumps and total reflection at critical incidence angles
validation: Exact energy-conservation verification (|R|^2 + impedance*|T|^2 = 1) and reduction to classical welded-interface Fresnel-like SH formulas
stated_limitations: Isothermal scalar SH polarization only (no P-SV mode conversion)
future_work: Extend non-ideal strain-gradient interphase wave scattering to coupled in-plane P-SV waves

title: Investigation of SH wave propagation in piezoelectric plates
authors: Mouldi Zagrouba; Mohamed Shili Bouhdima
model_constitutive: Linear anisotropic/orthotropic/6mm piezoelectricity under quasi-electrostatic approximation
geometry: Homogeneous and functionally graded piezoelectric plate of finite thickness h under electrically open and shorted surface boundary conditions
method: Power Series Technique (PST) expanding through-thickness SH displacement and electric potential in polynomial series to convert PDEs + BCs into an algebraic eigenvalue problem
main_result: Computes multi-mode SH dispersion curves, electromechanical coupling factors K^2, and through-thickness mode shapes rapidly via PST, categorizing material parameters into phase-velocity-increasing (c_44, e_15) vs decreasing (rho, epsilon_11, h) groups
validation: Verified to high precision against exact analytical transcendental dispersion curves for homogeneous PZT-4 plates
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear antiplane SH modes only
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Influence of irregular geologies and inhomogeneity on SH-wave propagation
authors: Rupinderjit Kaur; Sumit Kumar Vishwakarma; Tapas Ranjan Panigrahi
model_constitutive: Biot gravity-prestressed incremental elastodynamics for a heterogeneous Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic crustal layer overlying a heterogeneous elastic half-space
geometry: Crustal layer over semi-infinite half-space featuring localized interface topography notches (rectangular, parabolic, triangular, and combined irregularities)
method: Fourier transform + Willis/perturbation boundary-irregularity expansion + Whittaker function depth integration yielding closed-form complex Love-wave dispersion equation
main_result: Quantifies how Biot gravity parameter, viscoelastic damping, depth inhomogeneity, and notch geometry (types I-IV) shift SH phase and damped velocities
validation: Reduces to classical flat-interface homogeneous Love-wave dispersion when irregularity depth, gravity, viscosity, and heterogeneity vanish
stated_limitations: First-order small-slope perturbation in irregularity amplitude; isothermal antiplane SH mode only
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Three-dimensional nonlocal anisotropic elasticity: a generalized continuum theory of Angstrom-mechanics
authors: Markus Lazar; Eleni Agiasofitou; Giacomo Po
model_constitutive: 3D Eringen nonlocal anisotropic elasticity of generalized Helmholtz type L = 1 - Lambda_ij d_i d_j (with symmetric positive-definite 2nd-rank length-scale tensor Lambda_ij classified across all 8 crystal symmetry classes from triclinic to isotropic)
geometry: Unbounded 3D anisotropic crystals (cubic, hexagonal, orthorhombic, monoclinic, triclinic) containing straight/curved dislocation loops and point defects
method: Exact 3D Fourier-transform derivation of the anisotropic Yukawa-type Helmholtz Green-function kernel G(R) using crystal-class-adapted length-scale tensors calibrated to atomistic lattice/DFT phonon dispersion, applied to 3D Burgers/Mura dislocation integrals
main_result: Derives the exact 3D anisotropic Helmholtz nonlocal kernel G(x) = exp(-sqrt(x.Lambda^-1.x)) / (4*pi*sqrt(det Lambda)*sqrt(x.Lambda^-1.x)), classifies independent length-scale parameters (1 cubic, 2 hexagonal, 3 orthorhombic, 4 monoclinic, 6 triclinic), and obtains completely nonsingular 3D anisotropic Peach-Koehler dislocation stress, strain, and self-energy fields down to the Angstrom core
validation: Calibrated and validated against atomistic/MD/DFT dislocation core fields and phonon dispersion in cubic/hexagonal metals (Al, Cu, W, Fe, Mg)
stated_limitations: Static isothermal infinite-space 3D theory (explicitly utilizes whole-space R^3 Green's function so no boundary-surface integrals arise)
future_work: Implement nonsingular 3D anisotropic nonlocal dislocation fields into 3D Discrete Dislocation Dynamics (DDD) codes and extend to dynamic/bounded defect mechanics

title: Exact solutions for free vibrations of axially inhomogeneous Timoshenko beams with variable cross section
authors: Jianghong Yuan; Yih-Hsing Pao; Weiqiu Chen
model_constitutive: Classical local linear Timoshenko beam theory with simultaneous axial material grading E(x), G(x), rho(x) and variable cross-sectional geometry A(x), I(x)
geometry: Axially non-uniform functionally graded 1D Timoshenko beams under arbitrary classical end supports
method: Exact operator-factorization decoupling of the coupled variable-coefficient Timoshenko PDEs into two uncoupled second-order Sturm-Liouville ODEs under functional-proportionality conditions
main_result: Identifies a broad analytical class of axially inhomogeneous variable-section Timoshenko beams whose coupled motion equations decouple exactly into solvable Bessel/hypergeometric Sturm-Liouville equations, yielding exact benchmark eigenfrequencies
validation: Verified against uniform Timoshenko beam roots and independent numerical FEM/differential-quadrature solutions
stated_limitations: Exact decoupling requires an algebraic compatibility relation between axial stiffness, shear stiffness, and inertia profiles; isothermal local elasticity
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Love waves propagation in a piezoelectric layered structure with initial stresses
authors: Z. Qian; F. Jin; Z. Wang; K. Kishimoto
model_constitutive: Linearized incremental electroelasticity for an isotropic elastic guiding layer carrying depth-inhomogeneous initial stress sigma_0(x) bonded to a transversely isotropic 6mm piezoelectric half-space
geometry: SiO2/PMMA isotropic layer of finite thickness h with inhomogeneous residual stress on a polarized PZT/ZnO piezoelectric substrate under open/shorted electrical BCs
method: WKBJ asymptotic / power-series depth solution in the inhomogeneously prestressed layer matched to evanescent Bleustein-Gulyaev substrate potentials
main_result: Shows both constant and depth-graded manufacturing residual stresses significantly alter Love-wave phase velocity, group velocity, and electromechanical coupling factor K^2 across modes
validation: Recovers stress-free piezoelectric Love-wave benchmarks (Curtis-Redwood / Jin et al.) when initial stress vanishes
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear incremental theory; WKBJ approximation assumes smooth initial-stress gradient
future_work: Account for inhomogeneous manufacturing thermal-mismatch stresses in layered SAW sensor calibration

title: Propagation of SH waves in an irregular monoclinic crustal layer
authors: A. Chattopadhyay; S. Gupta; V. K. Sharma; Pato Kumari
model_constitutive: Classical linear anisotropic (monoclinic crystal/rock symmetry with 13 elastic constants, C_44, C_45, C_55 active for SH) elastodynamics over an isotropic half-space
geometry: Monoclinic crustal layer of mean thickness H with a rectangular interface irregularity of depth H' overlying a homogeneous isotropic elastic half-space
method: Fourier integral transform + Eringen-Samuels small-irregularity perturbation + Willis contour asymptotic evaluation yielding explicit perturbed Love-wave dispersion equation
main_result: Derives closed-form SH dispersion relation showing monoclinic anisotropy (C_45 cross-shear coupling) and rectangular crustal thickening lower dimensionless wavenumber kH for a given phase speed relative to flat isotropic layers
validation: Reduces exactly to classical isotropic Love-wave dispersion tan(k*H*s_1) = (mu_2*s_2)/(mu_1*s_1) when monoclinic off-diagonal terms and H'/H vanish
stated_limitations: First-order perturbation in irregularity depth H'/H << 1; isothermal elastic antiplane SH waves only
future_work: Extended in subsequent work (Chattopadhyay et al. 2010) to non-homogeneous monoclinic layers over monoclinic half-spaces

title: Influence of Boundaries on the Dispersion of Rayleigh Waves in a Functionally Graded Pre-Stressed Orthotropic Substrate
authors: Y. B. Darhas; N. Pradhan; S. Saha; A. Senapati; S. Pramanik
model_constitutive: Biot incremental 2D plane-strain elastodynamics for pre-stressed orthotropic functionally graded materials with exponential and logarithmic depth gradation profiles
geometry: Semi-infinite functionally graded pre-stressed orthotropic half-space under both traction-free and rigid-clamped surface boundary conditions
method: Analytical/WKB-like complex secular determinant formulation for 2D P-SV evanescent modes under exponential vs logarithmic stiffness/density grading
main_result: Compares Rayleigh-type dispersion and spatial attenuation across exponential vs logarithmic FGM profiles, initial stress levels, and stress-free vs rigid boundaries, finding monotonic decreases in phase velocity and attenuation with increasing gradation steepness
validation: Recovers classical homogeneous orthotropic and isotropic Rayleigh wave secular equations as gradation and pre-stress vanish
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear elastic FGM model without viscoelastic or thermoelastic coupling
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Propagation of SH Waves in an Irregular Non Homogeneous Monoclinic Crustal Layer over a Semi-Infinite Monoclinic Medium
authors: A. Chattopadhyay; S. Gupta; A. K. Singh; S. A. Sahu
model_constitutive: Linear monoclinic elastodynamics with depth-varying stiffness and density in the upper crustal layer over a homogeneous monoclinic half-space
geometry: Non-homogeneous monoclinic crustal layer with parabolic/rectangular interface irregularity overlying a semi-infinite monoclinic elastic medium
method: Fourier transform + Eringen-Samuels perturbation + Whittaker/Willis asymptotic integration yielding closed-form SH dispersion relation
main_result: Generalizes irregular-layer Love-wave dispersion to doubly monoclinic heterogeneous media, showing crustal non-homogeneity and deeper interface irregularity lower dimensionless phase velocity c/beta_1
validation: Reduces to Chattopadhyay et al. (2008) and classical isotropic Love dispersion in homogeneous/isotropic flat limits
stated_limitations: First-order perturbation in interface irregularity amplitude; isothermal antiplane SH mode only
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Surface waves in a general anisotropic poroelastic solid half-space
authors: M. D. Sharma
model_constitutive: Biot linear general anisotropic (triclinic, 21 skeleton + 6 solid-fluid + 1 fluid + 6 inertial tortuosity constants) non-dissipative poroelasticity
geometry: Semi-infinite general anisotropic fluid-saturated poroelastic half-space with open-pore or sealed-pore traction-free plane boundary
method: 8th-order Christoffel polynomial partial-wave superposition (4 attenuating quasi-P1, quasi-P2, quasi-S1, quasi-S2 modes) yielding an explicit complex secular equation for directional Rayleigh-type surface waves
main_result: Derives the general triclinic poroelastic surface-wave secular equation and computes azimuthal phase-velocity polar diagrams in orthorhombic, monoclinic, and triclinic water-saturated paragneiss, showing stronger anisotropy shrinks angular sectors admitting true non-leaky surface waves
validation: Consistent reductions across orthorhombic -> monoclinic -> triclinic symmetries and dry anisotropic Barnett-Lothe / Currie limits
stated_limitations: Assumes non-dissipative (inviscid pore fluid) regime so secular roots are searched along real slowness; isothermal
future_work: Include viscous Darcy pore-fluid dissipation (leaky/attenuated complex slowness) and layered anisotropic poroelasticity

title: Negative refraction of elastic waves at the deep-subwavelength scale in a single-phase metamaterial
authors: R. Zhu; X. N. Liu; G. K. Hu; C. T. Sun; G. L. Huang
model_constitutive: Single-phase chiral locally resonant stainless-steel elastic metamaterial exhibiting simultaneous translational-rotational resonances (negative effective mass density AND negative effective elastic modulus in a subwavelength passband)
geometry: 2D wedge/prism of CNC-machined chiral stainless-steel unit cells (lattice constant ~1/15 of host wavelength) coupled to a homogeneous stainless-steel plate
method: Bloch-Floquet equifrequency contour (EFC) and effective-medium retrieval, full-wave FEM, and scanning laser Doppler vibrometer ultrasonic wedge-refraction experiments
main_result: Demonstrates deep-subwavelength negative refraction (theta_r = -37 deg, opposite group and phase velocities) and disorder-tolerant wave steering of coupled elastic waves in a monolithic single-phase chiral solid metamaterial
validation: Direct 2D laser vibrometer experimental wavefield mapping matching FEM simulations and equifrequency-contour Snell predictions
stated_limitations: Narrowband operation near local chiral resonance (~42-45 kHz) with chiral EFC anisotropy and longitudinal/transverse interface mode conversion
future_work: Exploit single-phase chiral metamaterials for subwavelength elastic flat lenses and robust structural waveguiding

title: Screw dislocation in nonlocal anisotropic elasticity
authors: Markus Lazar; Eleni Agiasofitou
model_constitutive: 2D Eringen nonlocal anisotropic antiplane elasticity with twofold anisotropy (anisotropic elastic moduli C_44, C_45, C_55 AND 2D anisotropic Helmholtz length-scale operator L = 1 - (l_1^2 d_x^2 + 2*l_12 d_x d_y + l_2^2 d_y^2))
geometry: Unbounded 3D crystal containing a straight screw dislocation along the z-axis (hexagonal basal/prismatic, cubic, and monoclinic orientations)
method: Derivation of the exact 2D anisotropic modified-Bessel K_0 nonlocal kernel as the Green's function of the 2D anisotropic Helmholtz operator, convolved analytically with classical Stroh/anisotropic screw-dislocation stress fields
main_result: Obtains simple closed-form nonsingular stress fields (in terms of K_1 Bessel functions) for straight screw dislocations in general anisotropic crystals with 3 directional nonlocal length parameters, eliminating the classical 1/r core singularity
validation: Exact reduction to Eringen's (1977) isotropic nonlocal screw dislocation (when C_44=C_55=mu, C_45=0, l_1=l_2=e_0*a) and classical anisotropic elasticity as l_ij -> 0
stated_limitations: 2D static antiplane straight screw dislocation in unbounded space (later generalized to full 3D anisotropic curved dislocations in Lazar, Agiasofitou & Po 2020)
future_work: Extend anisotropic Helmholtz nonlocal kernels to edge dislocations, 3D defect loops, and atomistic core calibration

title: Introduction to Biot's theory of poroelastic wave propagation
authors: Masao Kimura
model_constitutive: Tutorial review of Biot's (1956, 1962) isotropic linear poroelastodynamics written in the solid-displacement / relative-fluid-displacement (u - w) formulation with Johnson-Koplik-Dashen dynamic viscous permeability correction F(omega)
geometry: Unbounded 3D water-saturated isotropic porous medium (silica sand)
method: Step-by-step pedagogical derivation of Biot-Stoll moduli (H, C, M), dynamic tortuosity/viscosity transition frequencies (f_t, f_c), and biquadratic fast/slow compressional + shear dispersion relations
main_result: Presents a clean self-contained u-w formulation of Biot poroelastic wave speeds and attenuations, illustrating viscous-to-inertial transition dispersion in water-saturated silica sand from 1 Hz to 1 MHz
validation: Reproduces standard Biot-Stoll water-saturated sand phase-speed and attenuation curves across characteristic frequencies f_t = 86 Hz and f_c = 559 Hz
stated_limitations: Introductory tutorial restricted to homogeneous isotropic isothermal saturated media
future_work: Serve as theoretical baseline for marine-sediment, bone, and sound-absorbing poroacoustics

title: Arching effect in sand piles under base deflection using geometrically non-linear isogeometric analysis
authors: Tan Nguyen; Loc V. Tran
model_constitutive: Off-topic geotechnical computational mechanics: geometrically nonlinear Total-Lagrangian elastoplastic (Mohr-Coulomb) continuum modeling of granular sand piles
geometry: 2D planar wedge and 3D axisymmetric conical sand piles subjected to staged construction gravity loading and downward base deflection
method: Higher-order NURBS Isogeometric Analysis (IGA) coupled with return-mapping Mohr-Coulomb plasticity and arc-length/Newton-Raphson nonlinear solvers
main_result: Captures Terzaghi granular arching and centerline vertical-pressure dip under base deflection, showing conical sand piles exhibit stronger stress redistribution than planar wedges and finite-strain nonlinearity softens the stress dip above 5% base deflection
validation: Benchmarked against classical Smid-Novosad sand-pile pressure-dip experiments and finite-element literature (Ai et al. 2013)
stated_limitations: Off-topic quasi-static geotechnical sand-pile plasticity paper
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Study on the mechanical characteristics of a fibre reinforced flexible pipe under radial compression loads
authors: Zhenwen Sun; Weiping Huang; Hailong Lu; Jun Yan; Yuanchao Yin; Yufeng Bu
model_constitutive: Off-topic ocean-engineering structural mechanics: analytical curved-beam / orthotropic cylindrical-ring radial stiffness theory and 3D ABAQUS multi-layer contact FEA of bonded/unbonded glass/carbon fiber-reinforced flexible marine pipes
geometry: Multi-layer concentric polymeric/helical-fiber-reinforced flexible subsea pipe compressed radially between opposing tensioner platens
method: Castigliano energy derivation for orthotropic tube radial stiffness, laboratory radial crush testing of two pipe specimens, and 3D ABAQUS FEA
main_result: Derives closed-form radial compression stiffness agreeing within 8.7% (analytical) and 13.5% (3D FEA) of physical pipe compression tests
validation: Direct laboratory radial compression tests on two fabricated fiber-reinforced flexible pipe prototypes
stated_limitations: Off-topic static structural marine-pipe paper
future_work: Account for combined axial tension, internal pressure, and nonlinear interlayer slip during deepwater pipe laying

title: Wave propagation in a generalized thermoelastic solid cylinder of arbitrary cross-section
authors: P. Ponnusamy
journal: International Journal of Solids and Structures
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic Green-Lindsay temperature-rate-dependent generalized thermoelasticity (two relaxation times)
geometry: Infinitely long homogeneous thermoelastic solid cylinder of arbitrary smooth cross-section (specifically circular, elliptical, and Cassini-oval / rounded-polygonal waveguides) with traction-free thermally insulated lateral surface
method: Buchwald-type three-scalar-potential Helmholtz uncoupling in cylindrical coordinates (r, theta, z) satisfied along the irregular boundary via Nagaya's Fourier Expansion Collocation Method (FECM)
main_result: Computes dimensionless frequency-wavenumber dispersion curves for longitudinal and symmetric/antisymmetric flexural thermoelastic guided modes in elliptical and non-circular cylinders as a function of aspect ratio a/b
validation: Circular limit a/b = 1 verified against exact Pochhammer-Chree thermoelastic cylinder roots
stated_limitations: Homogeneous isotropic cylinder; Fourier collocation conditioning degrades for very high aspect ratios or sharp corners
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: A Continuum Theory of Elastic Material Surfaces (with 1975 Addenda)
authors: Morton E. Gurtin; A. Ian Murdoch
journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis (Vol. 57, pp. 291-323 & Vol. 59, pp. 389-390)
model_constitutive: Foundational finite-deformation and linearized Gurtin-Murdoch continuum theory of 2D elastic material surfaces/interfaces adhering to 3D elastic bodies with residual surface stress tensor sigma_0*I, surface Lame moduli (lambda_0, mu_0; refined in 1975 Addenda as mu_0 = mu - sigma_0, lambda_0 = lambda + sigma_0), and surface mass density rho_0
geometry: Arbitrary curved 2D smooth material boundary/interface S of a 3D body B; cleaved circular cylinder and half-space plane-wave reflection
method: Intrinsic surface differential geometry, Cauchy surface-traction theorem from force/moment balances, Noll frame-indifference & isotropy representations, linearization with non-zero residual surface tension, and uniqueness theorem
main_result: Establishes the rigorous nonlinear and linearized Gurtin-Murdoch equations (div_S S = T*n + rho_0*u_tt, S = sigma_0*I + (lambda_0+sigma_0)(tr E)I + 2*(mu_0-sigma_0)E + sigma_0*grad_S u), proves linearized uniqueness conditions, and corrects the pure-surface-tension limit (mu = lambda = 0) in the 1975 Addenda
validation: Axiomatic continuum-mechanical derivations, frame-indifference consistency, and recovery of Young-Laplace capillary jump for static fluid-like constant surface tension
stated_limitations: Purely mechanical isothermal theory (immiscible coherent surfaces without mass diffusion or thermal coupling — thermodynamic counterpart deferred to Murdoch 1976)
future_work: Extend to thermodynamic surface processes, solid-solid interfaces, surface wave waveguides, and surface couple stresses

title: Analytical solutions for elastic SH-waves propagating through an isotropic inhomogeneous layer
authors: M. Bednarik; M. Cervenka; P. Lotton; L. Simon
model_constitutive: Classical linear isotropic elastodynamics with continuously varying 1D shear modulus mu(x) and mass density rho(x) parameterized by 7-parameter triconfluent Heun solvability transformations
geometry: Finite-thickness 1D functionally graded isotropic layer (0 <= x <= L) embedded between two homogeneous acoustic/elastic half-spaces under obliquely incident SH plane waves
method: Liouville-Darboux coordinate/amplitude transformation mapping the variable-coefficient SH Helmholtz ODE onto the Triconfluent Heun Equation (THE), yielding exact closed-form triconfluent Heun and polynomial reflection/transmission matrices
main_result: Constructs a flexible 7-parameter family of smooth non-monotonic/monotonic FGM shear-modulus and density profiles admitting exact analytical SH reflection and transmission coefficients in terms of triconfluent Heun functions
validation: Verified to machine precision against 4th-order Runge-Kutta numerical ODE integration and exact energy conservation |R|^2 + (Z_1/Z_3)|T|^2 = 1
stated_limitations: Isothermal, lossless elastic scalar SH waves only
future_work: Apply exact 7-parameter Heun profiles to phononic-crystal unit-cell design and acoustic impedance matching layers

title: IV. On the Dynamical Theory of Gases
authors: J. Clerk Maxwell
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London
model_constitutive: Kinetic theory of inverse-fifth-power repulsive molecules (Maxwell molecules) introducing phenomenological viscoelastic stress relaxation dF/dt = E*ds/dt - F/T AND exact molecular moment-transfer equations for pressure tensor and third-order heat-flux relaxation
geometry: 3D rarefied/continuum monatomic and polyatomic gases, vertical gravity-stratified columns, diffusing gas mixtures, sheared layers, and heat-conducting slabs
method: Exact collision-integral transfer equation for arbitrary molecular velocity moments (simplified cleanly for r^-5 repulsion where collision rate is independent of relative speed)
main_result: Establishes the Maxwell viscoelastic relaxation law (relaxation time T = mu/E), derives the kinetic moment transport equations containing finite-relaxation-time stress and heat-flux rate terms (precursor to Cattaneo and Grad 13-moment equations), proves equilibrium temperature is independent of gravity height, and derives pressure-independent viscosity and thermal conductivity C = (5/(3*(gamma-1)))*(p_0/(rho_0*theta_0))*(mu/s)
validation: Quantitative comparison against Graham's gas-diffusion data, Maxwell/Stokes air viscosity measurements, and Forbes/Clausius thermal-conductivity ratios
stated_limitations: Exact analytical collision-integral simplification relies on inverse-fifth-power intermolecular force law; steady heat conduction drops transient heat-flux inertia term
future_work: Extend molecular collision transport analysis to general intermolecular force laws and polyatomic internal-energy exchange

title: Microscale Heat Conduction in Dielectric Thin Films
authors: A. Majumdar
journal: Journal of Heat Transfer (Transactions of the ASME)
model_constitutive: Equation of Phonon Radiative Transfer (EPRT) derived from the semiclassical phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation under frequency-dependent relaxation-time approximation tau(omega, T)
geometry: 1D dielectric thin film (diamond, silicon) of thickness L between boundary reservoirs at T_1 and T_2 across macroscale (L >> l) to ballistic (L << l) regimes
method: Transformation of directional phonon intensity I_omega(mu, x, t) into radiative-transfer integral-differential form solved via discrete-ordinates S_N quadrature across acoustic thickness xi = L/l
main_result: Establishes the foundational EPRT bridging Fourier conduction in acoustically thick films (L >> l), Stefan-Boltzmann-like T^4 phonon blackbody radiation in ballistic thin films (L << l), and hyperbolic wave-like heat-pulse propagation with radiative boundary slip under transient heating
validation: Steady-state diamond thin-film effective conductivity and boundary temperature jump compared against Flik-Tien geometric mean-free-path models and experimental diamond data
stated_limitations: Single relaxation-time approximation lumps momentum-conserving normal (N) and resistive umklapp/impurity (R) scattering together, missing pure second-sound hydrodynamics when tau_N << tau_R
future_work: Incorporate separate normal vs umklapp collision operators, polarization branches, and transient ultrafast laser film heating

title: New Fractional Derivatives with Nonlocal and Non-Singular Kernel: Theory and Application to Heat Transfer Model
authors: Abdon Atangana; Dumitru Baleanu
model_constitutive: Atangana-Baleanu Caputo (ABC) and Riemann-Liouville (ABR) fractional time derivatives of order alpha in [0, 1] replacing the singular power-law kernel (t-tau)^(-alpha) with the non-singular nonlocal Mittag-Leffler kernel E_alpha[-alpha*(t-tau)^alpha / (1-alpha)], applied to 1D rigid heat conduction
geometry: Time half-line t >= 0 and 1D heterogeneous/multi-scale heat-conducting medium
method: Laplace-transform operational properties, Lipschitz/Banach fixed-point uniqueness and existence analysis, and Crank-Nicolson-type numerical discretization
main_result: Introduces the Atangana-Baleanu (ABC and ABR) non-singular Mittag-Leffler kernel fractional derivatives (crossing over between stretched-exponential/Gaussian-like short-time behavior and power-law long-time memory, unlike single-exponential Caputo-Fabrizio) and applies them to anomalous heat transfer
validation: Exact Laplace-transform inversion identities recovering ordinary first derivative at alpha -> 1 and identity integral at alpha -> 0
stated_limitations: Purely scalar uncoupled heat-diffusion demonstration without thermodynamic Clausius-Duhem proof or mechanical coupling; initial-value compatibility restrictions at t = 0+ apply to ABC operators
future_work: Apply ABC/ABR Mittag-Leffler memory operators to multi-scale anomalous diffusion, viscoelasticity, and groundwater/thermal engineering

title: Nonlocal Continuum Field Theories
authors: A. Cemal Eringen
model_constitutive: Comprehensive nonlocal continuum field theory treatise covering spatial and memory-dependent nonlocal thermoelastic solids (Ch. 3.2, Ch. 6), nonlocal fluid dynamics (Ch. 7), nonlocal electrodynamics/superconductivity/piezoelectricity (Ch. 8-10), radiative/relativity extensions, and nonlocal micromorphic/micropolar continua (Ch. 13-14)
geometry: 3D bulk crystals (Brillouin zone), Rayleigh surface waves, screw/edge dislocations, Mode I/II/III Griffith cracks, microscopic fluid channels, and electromagnetic dispersive media
method: Axiom of attenuating neighborhood in H-norm, global Gibbsian/Clausius-Duhem nonlocal thermodynamics, Fourier/Laplace kernel matching to Born-von Karman lattice dynamics, and singular-free Wiener-Hopf/Fredholm crack & defect solutions
main_result: Unifies 30 years of Eringen's nonlocal field theories, showing Helmholtz-kernel differential approximations (1 - e_0^2*a^2*Laplacian)t_kl = sigma_kl match acoustic phonon dispersion, make Rayleigh waves dispersive, eliminate dislocation core and crack-tip stress singularities (predicting finite cohesive fracture toughness from atomic constants), and capture nanoscale channel viscosity changes
validation: Quantitative agreement against neutron-scattering phonon dispersion (Al, Si, diamond), MD dislocation cores, Griffith brittle fracture strength, and anomalous skin effect / Debye screening
stated_limitations: Differential Helmholtz operator equivalence (1 - l^2*Laplacian) holds rigorously on unbounded domains; bounded-domain integral-to-differential boundary conditions and space-time relativistic/wave-operator kernels remain subtle
future_work: Extend nonlocal memory-dependent thermoelectromechanical and microcontinuum models to nanoscale devices, biophysics, and dynamic fracture

title: Some Variational Principles for Coupled Thermoelasticity
authors: Francesco Marotti de Sciarra
model_constitutive: Time-discretized (backward finite-difference time-step) nonlinear/convex and linearized Green-Naghdi (Type II / Type III) coupled thermoelasticity with subdifferential/convex dissipation potentials
geometry: Arbitrary 3D bounded thermoelastic structural domain under mixed displacement/traction and thermal-displacement/entropy-flux boundary conditions
method: Convex analysis, Legendre-Fenchel conjugate potentials, and saddle-point / Hu-Washizu / Hellinger-Reissner-type multi-field variational principles over a finite time step
main_result: Constructs a hierarchy of four multi-field variational functionals (culminating in a strictly convex primal displacement + thermal-displacement functional) for incremental Green-Naghdi coupled thermoelastic BVPs, proving solution uniqueness from strict convexity
validation: Variational stationarity recovery of all field equations, constitutive laws, and mixed thermomechanical boundary conditions
stated_limitations: Applies to a time-stepped incremental BVP rather than continuous-time convolutional dynamics; author explicitly notes rigorous existence of solutions remains an open challenge
future_work: Establish functional-analytic existence proofs and finite-element implementations of the strictly convex GN variational principles

title: Computation of Propagating and Non-Propagating Lamb-Like Wave in a Functionally Graded Piezoelectric Spherical Curved Plate by an Orthogonal Function Technique
authors: Xiaoming Zhang; Shunli Liang; Xiaoming Han; Zhi Li
model_constitutive: 3D linear anisotropic functionally graded piezoelectricity (FGPM) in spherical coordinates (r, theta, phi) with arbitrary radial material grading
geometry: Radially functionally graded piezoelectric spherical curved plate/shell segment of finite thickness under traction-free open/shorted electrical surfaces
method: Legendre orthogonal polynomial expansion incorporating step/window boundary functions to convert coupled radial PDEs directly into a polynomial matrix eigenvalue problem in complex wavenumber k
main_result: Computes the complete 3D complex wavenumber dispersion spectrum (propagating real, purely imaginary, and complex evanescent Lamb-like branches) in FGPM spherical curved plates, quantifying curvature radius R/h and grading index effects on evanescent mode loops
validation: Verified in the large-radius flat-plate limit against published homogeneous and FGM piezoelectric plate dispersion curves
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear quasi-electrostatic model; high-frequency modes require larger orthogonal polynomial truncation order
future_work: Apply complex evanescent Lamb-mode spectra to ultrasonic NDE of curved smart composite shells

title: Recent advances in generalized thermoelasticity theory and the modified models: a review
authors: Farshad Shakeriaski; Maryam Ghodrat; Juan Escobedo-Diaz; Masud Behnia
journal: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering
model_constitutive: Broad engineering literature review of generalized thermoelasticity with second sound: Lord-Shulman (LS), Green-Lindsay (GL), Green-Naghdi (GN-II/III), Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL), Three-Phase-Lag (TPL), Multi-Phase-Lag (MPL), two-temperature, nonlocal, fractional, and memory-dependent derivative (MDD) thermoelasticity
geometry: 1D/2D/3D half-spaces, beams/plates/shells, cracked solids, porous/piezoelectric/magnetothermoelastic structures, and laser-heated films
method: Narrative classification of constitutive equations, analytical/FEM/BEM solution techniques, and engineering applications (ultrafast laser heating, shock waves, fracture)
main_result: Catalogs recent (2010-2020) modifications of generalized thermoelasticity, highlighting how higher-order phase lags, two-temperature couplings, and nonlocal/fractional extensions alter thermal shock stress peaks and wave attenuation
validation: Qualitative comparison of published numerical trends across LS, GL, GN, DPL, and TPL studies
stated_limitations: Purely descriptive compilation without independent recomputation, unified nondimensionalization, or critical stability/ill-posedness screening of high-order Taylor DPL/MPL truncations
future_work: Calls for 3D nonlinear generalized thermoelastic fracture/laser-ablation modeling, experimental measurement of relaxation times, and coupled multiphysics FEM/BEM solvers

title: The Computation of Complex Dispersion and Properties of Evanescent Lamb Wave in Functionally Graded Piezoelectric-Piezomagnetic Plates
authors: Xiaoming Zhang; Zhi Li; Jiangong Yu
model_constitutive: Linear 3D coupled magneto-electro-elasticity in through-thickness functionally graded piezoelectric-piezomagnetic (FGPPM, BaTiO3-CoFe2O4) plates
geometry: Infinite flat FGPPM plate of finite thickness h with traction-free electromagnetically open or shorted top/bottom surfaces
method: Legendre orthogonal polynomial series expansion reducing the variable-coefficient coupled 4-field (u_x, u_z, phi, psi) PDEs + BCs to a quadratic/quartic eigenvalue problem in complex wavenumber k
main_result: Computes for the first time the complete 3D complex dispersion spectrum (real propagating, purely imaginary, and complex evanescent Lamb modes) in FGPPM plates, mapping modal trajectory connections across cutoff frequencies and through-thickness Poynting power-flow vortices of evanescent modes
validation: Propagating real branches verified quantitatively against state-space / Peano-series benchmark solutions
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear local magneto-electro-elasticity
future_work: Exploit evanescent Lamb-mode edge resonances for ultrasonic NDE of magnetoelectric composite plates

title: On The Phase-Lag Green-Naghdi Thermoelasticity Theories
authors: Ahmed S. El-Karamany; Magdy A. Ezzat
model_constitutive: Three phase-lagged anisotropic inhomogeneous Green-Naghdi thermoelasticity theories: Single-Phase-Lag GN-III (equivalent to MGT thermoelasticity!), Dual-Phase-Lag GN-II, and Dual-Phase-Lag GN-III (first-order Taylor phase lags applied to q, grad(T), and grad(alpha))
geometry: General 3D inhomogeneous anisotropic bounded thermoelastic body for theorems; 1D homogeneous half-space under thermal shock for numerical Honig-Hirdes Laplace inversion
method: Unified heat-transport operator formulation, Laplace-domain convolutional reciprocity and variational principles, uniqueness and continuous-dependence theorems, and 1D half-space state-space numerical example
main_result: Introduces single- and dual-phase-lag modifications of GN-II and GN-III thermoelasticity to restore finite thermal wavefront speeds to GN-III (removing GN-III's diffusive infinite-speed component), proves uniqueness under parameter positivity inequalities (e.g., K*tau_q - K^* tau_alpha >= 0), and establishes convolutional variational/reciprocity theorems
validation: Reduces to Lord-Shulman, Green-Naghdi Type II, Green-Naghdi Type III, and Roy Choudhuri TPL as special parameter choices
stated_limitations: Relies on first-order Taylor expansion of phase lags; exponential stability vs blow-up (e.g., when K*tau_q < K^* as later proved by Quintanilla 2019 for MGT) is not fully characterized via semigroup spectrum here
future_work: Extend phase-lagged Green-Naghdi models to fractional, memory-dependent, and micropolar/piezoelectric continua

title: Energy analysis at the boundary interface of elastic and piezothermoelastic half-spaces
authors: M. S. Barak; R. Kumar; R. Kumar; V. Gupta
model_constitutive: 2D orthotropic Eringen spatial-differential nonlocal ((1 - e_0^2*a^2*nabla^2)sigma_ij = sigma_ij^L) piezothermoelasticity with Dual-Phase-Lag Memory-Dependent Derivatives (DPL-MDD, sliding window delay omega_0 and kernel K(t-xi)) and Hyperbolic/Classical/One-Temperature (HTT/CTT/OTT) conductive-thermodynamic temperature laws
geometry: Welded planar interface z = 0 between an isotropic local elastic half-space (ES) and a nonlocal orthotropic piezothermoelastic half-space (NPS) under obliquely incident P or SV harmonic waves
method: Harmonic plane-wave dispersion (2x2 in ES; 8th-order coupled qP, qSV, qT, eP potential polynomial in NPS), 6x6 interface boundary-condition matrix, and time-averaged energy-flux partition + interaction-energy balance check
main_result: Computes reflected (P, SV), transmitted (qP, qSV, qT, eP), and dissipative mode-interaction energy ratios vs incidence angle across HTT, CTT, and OTT models with and without MDD and Eringen spatial nonlocality, verifying total energy conservation
validation: Numerical verification that sum of reflected, transmitted, and interaction energy ratios equals unity at all angles, plus specialization to OTT, CTT, and local piezothermoelastic limits
stated_limitations: Applies unbounded differential Eringen operator directly up to the interface without integral constitutive boundary/interface conditions or space-time causal nonlocality (Lazar-Agiasofitou 2022), and combines DPL + MDD + HTT heuristically without proving IBVP semigroup stability
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Reflection/transmission of plane waves at the interface of an ideal fluid and nonlocal piezothermoelastic medium
authors: Vipin Gupta; Rajesh Kumar; Manjeet Kumar; Vijayata Pathania; M. S. Barak
journal: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow
model_constitutive: 2D orthotropic Eringen spatial-differential nonlocal piezothermoelasticity combining Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL), Memory-Dependent Derivatives (MDD), and Hyperbolic Two-Temperature (HTT / CTT / OTT) conduction coupled across a fluid-solid interface to an inviscid compressible acoustic fluid
geometry: Planar interface between an inviscid ideal fluid half-space (FHS) and a nonlocal orthotropic piezothermoelastic half-space (NOPHS) under an obliquely incident acoustic P wave
method: Harmonic plane-wave potential/eigenvalue expansion, inviscid slip + normal-traction/displacement + insulated/shorted interface system, and energy-flux partition + dissipative interaction-energy verification
main_result: Quantifies reflected fluid P-wave, transmitted solid (qP, qSV, qT, eP), and dissipative interaction energy ratios across incidence angles, comparing HTT, CTT, OTT, LS, DPL, MDD kernel choices, and nonlocal scale parameter
validation: Energy conservation check (sum of reflected, transmitted, and interaction energy ratios ~ 1 across 0-90 deg) and specialization to local, OTT, CTT, and LS limits
stated_limitations: Uses purely spatial differential Eringen nonlocality without interfacial constitutive boundary conditions or space-time causal nonlocality, assumes inviscid thermally uncoupled fluid, and lacks thermodynamic/semigroup stability proof for combined DPL-MDD-HTT parameters
future_work: Suggests material classification using hyperbolic two-temperature and MDD delay parameters for smart acoustic/sonar transducer interfaces
